results.rationale: The application implements an explicit existence check: WithdrawalProcess calls findById(...).orElseThrow and throws IllegalStateException 'Cannot find card with id ...' before any INSERT. The SQL trace (c05) shows only the SELECT. The failure surfaces as an unhandled HTTP 500 Internal Server Error, not a client-error rejection, so it counts as a pre-persistence failure, not an elegant application rejection. The database FK was never reached.
limitations: Database FK enforcement itself was not reached/observed.

Reclassified from APPLICATION_REJECTED: the pre-persistence rejection returns a generic HTTP 500 rather than an elegant client error, and the database constraint could not be reached through the API because of the application-side guard.

warnings: Targets were extracted with schema_context_id dbctx-2c246b7230ae (in-one-class/src/main/resources/schema.sql); deployed schema is exactly this file on H2 1.4.197.
H2 silently rounds values with scale > 2 for DECIMAL(18,2) columns instead of rejecting them.
The application accepts negative withdrawal amounts (balance check only), which is how precision overflows were reached; this is an app-logic weakness, not part of the extracted predicates.
Read-back used the H2 web console that the application itself exposes (spring.h2.console.enabled=true) on the permitted port.

Four targets (pc-d422ab0eead2, dep-6b92cefdf4cd, pc-73e9479cc046, pc-c93d051c414e) were reclassified as INCONCLUSIVE_PRE_PERSISTENCE_FAILURE. Their violations are stopped before persistence but surface as generic HTTP 500 errors.
